claim: GtACR1 is a light-gated anion channel discovered in 2015.
source: GtACR1 is a light-gated anion channel discovered in 2015 (Govorunova et al., 2015) now widely used in optogenetics as a neuron-silencing tool.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Govorunova et al., 2015.

claim: GtACR1 is widely used in optogenetics as a neuron-silencing tool.
source: GtACR1 is a light-gated anion channel discovered in 2015 (Govorunova et al., 2015) now widely used in optogenetics as a neuron-silencing tool.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in the field of optogenetics.

claim: GtACR1 conducts both bromide and chloride ions effectively.
source: GtACR1 conducts both bromide and chloride ions effectively with higher relative permeability for the former substrate (Govorunova et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Govorunova et al., 2015.

claim: GtACR1 has higher relative permeability for bromide than chloride.
source: GtACR1 conducts both bromide and chloride ions effectively with higher relative permeability for the former substrate (Govorunova et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Govorunova et al., 2015.

claim: The X-ray crystal structure of the dark (closed) form of GtACR1 homodimer was determined at 2.9 Å resolution.
source: We and the group of Karl Deisseroth independently determined X-ray crystal structures of the dark (closed) form of GtACR1 homodimer at 2.9 Å (Kim et al., 2018; Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2018 and Li et al., 2019.

claim: The conductance pathway of GtACR1 is attributable to a full-length intramolecular tunnel traversing each protomer from the extracellular side to the intracellular side of the membrane.
source: We proposed that the conductance pathway was attributable to a full-length intramolecular tunnel traversing each protomer from the extracellular side to the intracellular side of the membrane lined by mostly hydrophobic residues (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: The tunnel in GtACR1 is lined by mostly hydrophobic residues.
source: We proposed that the conductance pathway was attributable to a full-length intramolecular tunnel traversing each protomer from the extracellular side to the intracellular side of the membrane lined by mostly hydrophobic residues (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Current rectification by charges introduced inside but not outside the tunnel supports the hypothesis that the tunnel serves as the anion-conducting path upon photoactivation.
source: Current rectification by charges introduced inside but not outside the tunnel support our hypothesis that the tunnel serves as the anion-conducting path upon photoactivation (Sineshchekov et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sineshchekov et al., 2019.

claim: No substrate was found in the apo form structure of GtACR1 despite the presence of chloride in the crystallization conditions.
source: However, no substrate was found in either structure (Kim et al., 2018; Li et al., 2019) despite the presence of chloride in the crystallization conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2018 and Li et al., 2019.

claim: In the apo form of GtACR1, the tunnel is narrowed by three constrictions blocking ion permeation.
source: In the apo form (i.e., without anion substrate) (Li et al., 2019) the tunnel is narrowed by three constrictions blocking ion permeation: Constriction 1 (C1) in the extracellular half, C2 mid-membrane consisting of the photoactive retinylidene Schiff base and interacting residues, and C3 in the cytoplasmic half.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Constriction 1 (C1) is located in the extracellular half of the tunnel.
source: In the apo form (i.e., without anion substrate) (Li et al., 2019) the tunnel is narrowed by three constrictions blocking ion permeation: Constriction 1 (C1) in the extracellular half, C2 mid-membrane consisting of the photoactive retinylidene Schiff base and interacting residues, and C3 in the cytoplasmic half.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Constriction 2 (C2) is located mid-membrane and consists of the photoactive retinylidene Schiff base and interacting residues.
source: In the apo form (i.e., without anion substrate) (Li et al., 2019) the tunnel is narrowed by three constrictions blocking ion permeation: Constriction 1 (C1) in the extracellular half, C2 mid-membrane consisting of the photoactive retinylidene Schiff base and interacting residues, and C3 in the cytoplasmic half.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Constriction 3 (C3) is located in the cytoplasmic half of the tunnel.
source: In the apo form (i.e., without anion substrate) (Li et al., 2019) the tunnel is narrowed by three constrictions blocking ion permeation: Constriction 1 (C1) in the extracellular half, C2 mid-membrane consisting of the photoactive retinylidene Schiff base and interacting residues, and C3 in the cytoplasmic half.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Retinal photoisomerization at C2 needs to open all three constrictions to form a conductive anion channel through the protein.
source: In our model, retinal photoisomerization at C2 needs to open all three of these gates to form a conductive anion channel through the protein.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' proposed model.

claim: Bromide-bound GtACR1 crystals were obtained in the same conditions and pH used for the apo form structure, except for replacement of NaCl with NaBr.
source: Bromide-bound GtACR1 crystals were obtained in the same conditions and pH used for the apo form structure, except for replacement of NaCl with NaBr in both protein purification and crystallization buffers.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental conditions used in the study.

claim: The structure of bromide-bound GtACR1 was determined at 3.2 Å resolution by molecular replacement using the apo form structure (PDB code 6EDQ) as the model.
source: The structure of bromide-bound GtACR1 was determined at 3.2 Å resolution by molecular replacement (MR) using the apo form structure (PDB code 6EDQ) as the model (Table 1).
evidence: The claim describes the method used to determine the structure and references Table 1 for data.

claim: The bromide-bound GtACR1 exhibits a similar homodimeric overall structure as the apo form with an rmsd of approximately 0.6 Å.
source: The bromide-bound GtACR1 exhibits a similar homodimeric overall structure as the apo form (rmsd: ~0.6 Å by comparing Cα from residues 1 to 295) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison data and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: All 7-helices and trans-configured retinal moieties are well superimposed in the bromide-bound and apo structures.
source: All 7-helices and trans-configured retinal moieties are well superimposed, including the inter-subunit disulfide bridge stabilizing the N-terminus fragments of the two protomers on the extracellular surface.
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison data.

claim: The two protomers, chain A and chain B, are well superimposed with an rmsd of approximately 0.5 Å.
source: The two protomers, chain A and chain B, are also well superimposed with an rmsd of ~0.5 Å.
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison data.

claim: Each protomer exhibits a continuous tunnel extending from the extracellular to intracellular surfaces of the protein similar to that seen in the apo form structure.
source: Each protomer exhibits a continuous tunnel extending from the extracellular to intracellular surfaces of the protein similar to that seen in the apo form structure (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Bromide binding enlarges the tunnel in constriction C3 on the cytoplasmic side of the tunnel.
source: As seen from comparison of the tunnel profile diameters of the apo- and bromide-bound structures (Figure 1B–C), bromide binding enlarges the tunnel in constriction C3 on the cytoplasmic side of the tunnel, where it is bound (Figure 1A), and also in part of C2, adjacent to the binding site, and the more distant constriction C1 on the extracellular side of the tunnel.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of tunnel profiles shown in Figures 1B-C and 1A.

claim: Bromide binding enlarges the tunnel in part of C2, adjacent to the binding site.
source: As seen from comparison of the tunnel profile diameters of the apo- and bromide-bound structures (Figure 1B–C), bromide binding enlarges the tunnel in constriction C3 on the cytoplasmic side of the tunnel, where it is bound (Figure 1A), and also in part of C2, adjacent to the binding site, and the more distant constriction C1 on the extracellular side of the tunnel.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of tunnel profiles shown in Figures 1B-C and 1A.

claim: Bromide binding enlarges the tunnel in the more distant constriction C1 on the extracellular side of the tunnel.
source: As seen from comparison of the tunnel profile diameters of the apo- and bromide-bound structures (Figure 1B–C), bromide binding enlarges the tunnel in constriction C3 on the cytoplasmic side of the tunnel, where it is bound (Figure 1A), and also in part of C2, adjacent to the binding site, and the more distant constriction C1 on the extracellular side of the tunnel.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of tunnel profiles shown in Figures 1B-C and 1A.

claim: The widened constriction regions indicate a pre-activated conformation exhibiting a closed channel with fractional transition to an open-channel state.
source: The widened constriction regions indicate a pre-activated conformation exhibiting a closed channel with fractional transition to an open-channel state.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: The changes in chain A are more profound than in chain B, particularly near C1.
source: Despite the similar tunnel profiles of the two protomers, the changes in chain A (Figure 1B) are more profound than in chain B (Figure 1C), particularly near C1, indicating conformational differences between the tunnels of the two chains.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of tunnel profiles shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: A bromide ion was found at the cytoplasmic port of the tunnel in each protomer.
source: A bromide ion was found at the cytoplasmic port of the tunnel in each protomer (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The signal of bromide in chain A is stronger than in chain B based on the composite omit map.
source: Based on the composite omit map, the signal of bromide in chain A is stronger than in chain B (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is based on electron density map data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Refinement with a water molecule at the bromide position showed a strong positive electron density in the Fo-Fc difference map.
source: A priori, given the larger number of electrons in Br (Z = 35), it would be difficult to mistake it for a water molecule (Z = 10), but to test this possibility directly, the bromide ion was replaced with a water molecule and the structure refined using PHENIX (Adams et al., 2010). The refinement showed a strong positive electron density at the bromide position in the Fo-Fc difference map (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D) and it was diminished only when a bromide ion was placed at that position (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: The claim is based on refinement data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D.

claim: The positive electron density was diminished only when a bromide ion was placed at that position.
source: The refinement showed a strong positive electron density at the bromide position in the Fo-Fc difference map (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D) and it was diminished only when a bromide ion was placed at that position (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: The claim is based on refinement data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: The bromide-binding site is formed by three cyclic residues: Pro58, Trp246, and Trp250.
source: The bromide-binding site is formed by three cyclic residues: Pro58 from the cytoplasmic loop between TM1 and 2, and Trp246 and Trp250 from TM7 in a triangular configuration (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Pro58 is from the cytoplasmic loop between TM1 and 2.
source: The bromide-binding site is formed by three cyclic residues: Pro58 from the cytoplasmic loop between TM1 and 2, and Trp246 and Trp250 from TM7 in a triangular configuration (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Trp246 and Trp250 are from TM7.
source: The bromide-binding site is formed by three cyclic residues: Pro58 from the cytoplasmic loop between TM1 and 2, and Trp246 and Trp250 from TM7 in a triangular configuration (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In the binding site, a bromide is stabilized by a H-bond interaction formed by the indole NH group of Trp250.
source: In the binding site, a bromide is stabilized by a H-bond interaction formed by the indole NH group of Trp250.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the binding site.

claim: This type of anion binding conformation has been found in several chloride-bound nucleotide structures.
source: This type of anion binding conformation has also been found in several chloride-bound nucleotide structures (Auffinger et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Auffinger et al., 2004.

claim: Pro58 presses its ring towards the bromide anion with a distance of 3.6 Å and 3.1 Å between the bromide ion and CG and CD atoms of Pro58 in chain A.
source: Pro58 may play an important role in substrate binding by pressing its ring towards the bromide anion with a distance of 3.6 Å and 3.1 Å between the bromide ion and CG and CD atoms of Pro58 in chain A and 4.0 Å and 3.2 Å in chain B.
evidence: The claim is based on structural measurements.

claim: Pro58 presses its ring towards the bromide anion with a distance of 4.0 Å and 3.2 Å between the bromide ion and CG and CD atoms of Pro58 in chain B.
source: Pro58 may play an important role in substrate binding by pressing its ring towards the bromide anion with a distance of 3.6 Å and 3.1 Å between the bromide ion and CG and CD atoms of Pro58 in chain A and 4.0 Å and 3.2 Å in chain B.
evidence: The claim is based on structural measurements.

claim: The ring of proline exhibits a partial positive charge due to electron withdrawal by the adjacent protein backbone and the lower electronegativity of the hydrogens on the ring surface.
source: Unlike other aromatic residues, the ring of proline exhibits a partial positive charge due to electron withdrawal by the adjacent protein backbone and the lower electronegativity of the hydrogens on the ring surface (Zondlo, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zondlo, 2013.

claim: The partial electropositivity of Pro58 may contribute to the binding of bromide via electrostatic interactions.
source: The partial electropositivity of Pro58 may contribute to the binding of bromide via electrostatic interactions.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the structural and chemical properties of Pro58.

claim: This type of proline-halide interaction has been observed in the structure of the chloride-pump rhodopsin ClR (site 2).
source: Notably, this type of proline-halide interaction has also been observed in the structure of the chloride-pump rhodopsin ClR (site 2) (Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2016.

claim: Substitution of Pro58 by Glu reduced photocurrent amplitude, altered the kinetics of channel closing, and caused strong outward rectification of the current-voltage dependence.
source: Our previous results implicated Pro58 in gating of GtACR1, in that substitution of Pro58 by Glu reduced photocurrent amplitude, altered the kinetics of channel closing, and caused strong outward rectification of the current-voltage dependence (Li et al., 2019; Sineshchekov et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019 and Sineshchekov et al., 2019.

claim: Similar effects were observed in W246E and W250E mutants in the bromide-binding site.
source: We observed similar effects in W246E and W250E mutants in the bromide-binding site (Figure 2B), in that photocurrent amplitudes were significantly reduced compared to the wild type and outward rectification was increased (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Photocurrent amplitudes were significantly reduced in W246E and W250E mutants compared to the wild type.
source: We observed similar effects in W246E and W250E mutants in the bromide-binding site (Figure 2B), in that photocurrent amplitudes were significantly reduced compared to the wild type and outward rectification was increased (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Outward rectification was increased in W246E and W250E mutants.
source: We observed similar effects in W246E and W250E mutants in the bromide-binding site (Figure 2B), in that photocurrent amplitudes were significantly reduced compared to the wild type and outward rectification was increased (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: None of the three substitutions with Glu (P58E, W246E, W250E) reduced the selectivity for anions, as assessed by reversal potential measurements.
source: None of these three substitutions with Glu reduced the selectivity for anions, as assessed by reversal potential measurements (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Trp250 is close to the anion and forms an H-bond interaction between its indole NH and the bromide.
source: Based on the structure, the two tryptophan residues, Trp246 and Trp250, appear to have different roles in bromide binding; for example, compared to distant Trp246 moving its aromatic ring away from the bromide, Trp250 is close to the anion and forms an H-bond interaction between its indole NH and the bromide.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis.

claim: Trp246 moves its aromatic ring away from the bromide.
source: Based on the structure, the two tryptophan residues, Trp246 and Trp250, appear to have different roles in bromide binding; for example, compared to distant Trp246 moving its aromatic ring away from the bromide, Trp250 is close to the anion and forms an H-bond interaction between its indole NH and the bromide.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis.

claim: W250F shows reduction of the current amplitude by 50%.
source: In further examination of this bromide binding conformation, we found that W250F shows reduction of the current amplitude by 50%, whereas W246F behaves like WT (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: W246F behaves like WT.
source: In further examination of this bromide binding conformation, we found that W250F shows reduction of the current amplitude by 50%, whereas W246F behaves like WT (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: These results are consistent with the structural observations in which Trp250, but not Trp246, stabilizes bromide via H-bond interaction.
source: These results are consistent with the structural observations in which Trp250, but not Trp246, stabilizes bromide via H-bond interaction.
evidence: The claim is an inference connecting experimental results with structural observations.

claim: FTIR difference spectra of GtACR1 membranes recorded at 80 K reflect the photoinduced transition from the dark ground state to K and L-like intermediates formed upon illumination.
source: As previously shown, FTIR difference spectra of GtACR1 membranes recorded at 80 K reflect the photoinduced transition from the dark ground state to K and L-like intermediates formed upon illumination (Yi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yi et al., 2017.

claim: Negative bands in the FTIR spectra measure vibrational frequencies of normal modes in the dark state structure.
source: Negative bands in the spectra measure vibrational frequencies of normal modes in the dark state structure, whereas positive bands measure photoinduced appearance of altered vibrational frequencies in the photoproducts.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge of FTIR spectroscopy.

claim: Positive bands in the FTIR spectra measure photoinduced appearance of altered vibrational frequencies in the photoproducts.
source: Negative bands in the spectra measure vibrational frequencies of normal modes in the dark state structure, whereas positive bands measure photoinduced appearance of altered vibrational frequencies in the photoproducts.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge of FTIR spectroscopy.

claim: The major bands in the 1500–1600 cm−1 region reflect the ethylenic (C=C) stretch mode of the retinylidene chromophore in GtACR1.
source: The major bands in the 1500–1600 cm−1 region reflect the ethylenic (C=C) stretch mode of the retinylidene chromophore in GtACR1 (Yi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yi et al., 2017.

claim: Changes in γC=C in microbial rhodopsins entail alterations in the electron conjugation of the retinylidene polyene chain.
source: Changes in γC=C in microbial rhodopsins entail alterations in the electron conjugation of the retinylidene polyene chain (Bergo et al., 2004; Bergo et al., 2002; Bergo et al., 2003; Smith et al., 1987a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bergo et al., 2004; Bergo et al., 2002; Bergo et al., 2003; Smith et al., 1987a.

claim: The frequency of the negative ethylenic band (γC=C) undergoes an upshift from 1529 cm−1 in NaF to 1533 cm−1 in NaBr.
source: Notably, the frequency of the negative ethylenic band (γC=C) undergoes an upshift from 1529 cm−1 in NaF to 1533 cm−1 in NaBr (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is based on FTIR spectroscopy data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The significant upward shift of 3 and 4 cm−1 from that of Cl- and F-, respectively, by Br- in the dark state provides compelling evidence for Br- binding in the dark.
source: The significant upward shift of 3 and 4 cm−1 from that of Cl- and F-, respectively, by Br- in the dark state, provides compelling evidence for Br- binding in the dark.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on FTIR spectroscopy data.

claim: This Br- induced shift reveals an alteration in charge conjugation in the polyene chain of the retinylidene chromophore due to Br- binding.
source: This Br- induced shift reveals an alteration in charge conjugation in the polyene chain of the retinylidene chromophore due to Br- binding.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on FTIR spectroscopy data.

claim: Br- interacts with GtACR1 in the unilluminated ground state.
source: We conclude that Br- interacts with GtACR1 in the unilluminated ground state.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on FTIR spectroscopy data.

claim: The all-trans to 13-cis isomerization that occurs upon light absorption and induces formation of the K and L-like intermediates appears to be unaffected by different halides.
source: While the different halides alter the retinylidene γC=C band in the dark and L-like states, the all-trans to 13-cis isomerization that occurs upon light absorption and induces formation of the K and L-like intermediates appears to be unaffected.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on FTIR spectroscopy data.

claim: The unperturbed photoisomerization reaction is consistent with the photocurrent function observed with each of the three halides.
source: The unperturbed photoisomerization reaction, consistent with the photocurrent function observed with each of the three halides (Govorunova et al., 2015), is indicated by the absence of frequency shift differences in the negative and positive bands in the mixed C-C stretch fingerprint region from 1100 to 1300 cm−1 for the different halides (Figure 3) since these band frequencies (γC-C) are highly sensitive to the retinal isomeric configuration (Smith et al., 1987a; Smith et al., 1987b).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on FTIR spectroscopy data and supported by citations.

claim: Band frequencies (γC-C) are highly sensitive to the retinal isomeric configuration.
source: The unperturbed photoisomerization reaction, consistent with the photocurrent function observed with each of the three halides (Govorunova et al., 2015), is indicated by the absence of frequency shift differences in the negative and positive bands in the mixed C-C stretch fingerprint region from 1100 to 1300 cm−1 for the different halides (Figure 3) since these band frequencies (γC-C) are highly sensitive to the retinal isomeric configuration (Smith et al., 1987a; Smith et al., 1987b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Smith et al., 1987a and Smith et al., 1987b.

claim: In the apo form structure, Pro58, together with Leu108, Ala61, and Leu245, constrains the cytoplasmic port, leading to the cytoplasmic half of the tunnel narrowing to 3.6 Å in diameter.
source: In the apo form structure, Pro58, together with Leu108, Ala61, and Leu245, constrains the cytoplasmic port, leading to the cytoplasmic half of the tunnel narrowing to 3.6 Å in diameter (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: In the bromide-bound structure, the presence of bromide pushes Pro58 outward by approximately 1.8 Å.
source: In the bromide-bound structure, the presence of bromide pushes Pro58 outward by ~1.8 Å (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: As a result of Pro58 being pushed outward, the cytoplasmic half of the tunnel is broadened by 1 Å in diameter in both protomers.
source: As a result, the cytoplasmic half of the tunnel is broadened by 1 Å in diameter in both protomers (Figure 1B-C).
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison data shown in Figures 1B-C.

claim: In the apo form structure, the C1 constriction is stabilized by a salt-bridge formed between Arg94 and Glu223 near the extracellular surface.
source: In the apo form structure, the C1 constriction is stabilized by a salt-bridge formed between Arg94 and Glu223 near the extracellular surface (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: In the bromide-bound structure, chain B exhibits a similar conformation of C1 as that in the apo form.
source: In the bromide-bound structure, chain B exhibits a similar conformation of C1 as that in the apo form.
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison.

claim: In chain A of the bromide-bound structure, Arg94 undergoes salt-bridge switching along the tunnel.
source: In contrast, Arg94 undergoes salt-bridge switching along the tunnel in chain A (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The side-chain of Arg94 is flipped by approximately 180° to form an alternative salt-bridge with Asp234 in the photoactive site.
source: The side-chain of Arg94 is flipped by ~180o to form an alternative salt-bridge with Asp234 in the photoactive site (Figure 4A), resulting in modest relaxation (~1 Å in diameter) of the C1 constriction (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 1B.

claim: The salt-bridge switching of Arg94 results in modest relaxation (approximately 1 Å in diameter) of the C1 constriction.
source: The side-chain of Arg94 is flipped by ~180o to form an alternative salt-bridge with Asp234 in the photoactive site (Figure 4A), resulting in modest relaxation (~1 Å in diameter) of the C1 constriction (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on structural data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 1B.

claim: Arg94 is highly conserved in the microbial rhodopsin family.
source: Arg94 is highly conserved in the microbial rhodopsin family and it is critical for anion conductance of GtACR1.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge of microbial rhodopsins.

claim: Arg94 is critical for anion conductance of GtACR1.
source: Arg94 is highly conserved in the microbial rhodopsin family and it is critical for anion conductance of GtACR1.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: The mutation R94A or R94E nearly abolished anion conductance.
source: The mutation R94A or R94E nearly abolished anion conductance (Li et al., 2019; Sineshchekov et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019 and Sineshchekov et al., 2019.

claim: Arg94 is the only positively charged residue in the extracellular half of the tunnel.
source: Arg94 is the only positively charged residue in the extracellular half of the tunnel.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis.

claim: Arg94 may enable transfer of anions across the extracellular half of the tunnel via charge-charge interaction.
source: It may enable transfer of anions across the extracellular half of the tunnel via charge-charge interaction.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the structural and chemical properties of Arg94.

claim: The side chain rotation of Arg94 enables it and its neighboring residues to form a conformation nearly identical to the chloride-binding site of the Cl- pump ClR.
source: We found that this side chain rotation enables Arg94 and its neighboring residues to form a conformation nearly identical to the chloride-binding site of the Cl- pump ClR (Figure 4B).

claim: In the structure of ClR, a chloride ion (site 1) is bound between Arg95 and the Schiff base via H-bonds and salt-bridges.
source: In the structure of ClR, a chloride ion (site 1) is bound between Arg95 and the Schiff base via H-bonds and salt-bridges.

claim: Studies in three different laboratories have concluded that Asp234 is neutral in the dark state from measurements of the D234N mutant of GtACR1.
source: Studies in three different laboratories have concluded that Asp234 is neutral in the dark state from measurements of the D234N mutant of GtACR1 by UV-vis absorption spectroscopy (Kim et al., 2018; Sineshchekov et al., 2016), resonance Raman spectroscopy (Yi et al., 2016), and FTIR (Kim et al., 2018).

claim: The Asp234 residue is expected to be functionally important given its proximity to the PSB and its nearly universal conservation in microbial rhodopsins.
source: The Asp234 residue is expected to be functionally important given its proximity to the PSB and its nearly universal conservation in microbial rhodopsins.

claim: Kim et al., 2018 conducted an extensive analysis of Asp234 and report that the D234N mutation nearly abolished photocurrents.
source: Kim et al., 2018 conducted an extensive analysis of Asp234 and report that the D234N mutation nearly abolished photocurrents.

claim: Reduced photocurrents to 20% of wild-type from the D234N mutation were also observed by Sineshchekov et al., 2015.
source: Reduced photocurrents to 20% of wild-type from the D234N mutation were also observed by Sineshchekov et al., 2015.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sineshchekov et al., 2015.

claim: Differences in extent of photocurrent reduction are likely attributable to different assay conditions used in these studies.
source: Differences in extent of photocurrent reduction are likely attributable to different assay conditions used in these studies.

claim: The electrostatic interaction of Arg94 with Asp234 in the pre-activated state may be correlated with the change in the electron conjugation of the retinylidene polyene chain in the dark that was observed by FTIR.

claim: The identification of bromide at the cytoplasmic entry of the transmembrane tunnel provides direct evidence for the hypothesis that the tunnel is the closed anion channel.
source: We identified a novel bromide-binding site at the cytoplasmic entry of the transmembrane tunnel (Figure 1). The identification of bromide is supported by multiple lines of evidence: (1) the composite omit map indicates the presence of bromide at the cytoplasmic port (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B); (2) we exclude the possibility of a water at the bromide position as demonstrated in the Fo-Fc difference map (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D); (3) the bromide-binding site exhibits a similar chemical conformation seen in chloride-binding structures (Auffinger et al., 2004); (4) functional analysis of W250F and W246F is consistent with the H-bond interaction in the bromide-binding site (Figure 2B); (5) specific interaction of GtACR1 with bromide in the unphotolyzed dark state was further demonstrated by FTIR analysis (Figure 3). In sum, these data confirm the bromide binding conformation in the structure. These findings provide direct evidence for our hypothesis (Li et al., 2019) that the tunnel we observe both in the apo form and in an altered form in the bromide-bound condition, is the closed anion channel.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence including structural data, functional analysis, and FTIR analysis.
